newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer on large maturity.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer on large maturity.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Thursday as investors sought to reinvest an unusually large maturity of T-bills, with much of it going into the short end to the money market yield curve.
"There's a pretty large bill maturity today with the cash management bills maturing, so those funds are obviously being reemployed in the market," said one T-bill dealer with a Canadian bank.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.31 percent from 3.33 percent from the close of trading on Wednesday.
A total of C$7.9 billion of T-bills will mature today. The amount is unusually high because of a C$3.0 billion 35-day cash management T-bill auctioned on July 2.
Dealers said much of those funds are being reinvested in the short end, with the one-month T-bill rallying to yield 2.65 percent from 2.70 percent at Wednesday's close.
Weighing on the market is recent weakness in the currency, which yesterday softened towards C$1.39 (US$0.7194).
"The Canadian dollar weakening off has sort of made accounts a little bit cautious toward the longer end," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill strengthened to yield 3.71 percent from 3.72 percent on Wednesday.
The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 4.24 percent from 4.26 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.35 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
